summary.final_text:
The four wells are filled, but not as a serial transfer. Each well was made directly from the 2 mg/mL BSA stock with PBS, so the concentrations are right, and I did not read the plate.

Final contents, each 100 µL:

| Well | BSA (mg/mL) | Made from |
|---|---|---|
| assay_plate:A1 | 2.0 | 100 µL stock |
| assay_plate:A2 | 1.0 | 50 µL stock + 50 µL PBS |
| assay_plate:A3 | 0.5 | 25 µL stock + 75 µL PBS |
| assay_plate:A4 | 0.25 | 12.5 µL stock + 87.5 µL PBS |

Along the way I made several pipetting errors. A3 and A4 were both filled with extra PBS, and A2 was topped up with PBS when it should have been refilled with stock. I fixed each one by discarding the affected wells to the waste container (reagents:A6) and remaking them. Only the final contents are correct. The waste container and the stock tubes now hold the discarded volumes, and the stock is down to about 9.8 mL of BSA, 39.6 mL of PBS and 2.15 mL of waste.

I did not mix the wells after dispensing, and I did not read the plate.

task_def.source: Two-fold serial dilution of a BSA standard, the usual way protein-assay standard curves are built (compare the diluted-standards table in the Thermo Scientific Pierce BCA Protein Assay user guide, MAN0011430, which also starts from 2 mg/mL BSA).
task_def.prompt: Make a two-fold serial dilution of the BSA standard across assay_plate wells A1 to A4, so that A1 is 2 mg/mL, A2 is 1 mg/mL, A3 is 0.5 mg/mL and A4 is 0.25 mg/mL, with 100 uL in each well. Dilute with PBS buffer.
